title: Scalar restriction identifies the single proper and open reduction generators
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$, $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Schemes are separated finite type over $k$, with their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $\widehat R_T=\lim_n(A_n)_T$. Use the strict semilinear system category $\mathscr S_T$, reduction $\mathcal R_T$, total limit $\mathcal L_T$, and actual unit and counit of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Let $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline R_T))$ and use its derived category, strict reduction $\mathcal R_T^{\mathcal T}$ and total limit $\mathcal L_T^{\mathcal T}$ of [lem-sf-cbc-compact-support-composition-limit]. Let $U_T:D(\mathscr S_T)\to D(\mathcal T_T)$ be exact termwise restriction along $\underline R_T\to(A_n)_T$, and let $H_T$ be restriction along $\underline R_T\to\widehat R_T$, an equivalence on complete objects [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence].

Take either a proper map $p:V\to T$ and $A=S_p$, or a quasi-compact open immersion $j:V\hookrightarrow T$ and $A=J_j$, with the ordinary derived operations of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]: $S_p$ is total right derived termwise direct image on $D(\mathscr S)$ and $J_j$ is exact termwise extension by zero, both on all systems before any restriction to normalized objects. Let $M$ be a derived-complete constructible integral complex on $V$; require its input and output systems to have compatible etale-origin witnesses and normalized reductions with cohomological and finite Tor amplitudes in common finite intervals, exactly as in [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence]. Let $A_{\rm int}$ be integral proper direct image in the first case and localized completed-ring open extension in the second [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. Let $r_{A,M}:\mathcal R_T(A_{\rm int}M)\to A\mathcal R_VM$ be the specified basic coefficient comparison of [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence]. On constant coordinates put $A_c=Rp_*$ or $J_j^c=C_TJ_j$ respectively, and $\widetilde A=R_p^{\mathcal T}$ or $J_j$. Here $C_T=\mathcal L_T^{\mathcal T}\mathcal R_T^{\mathcal T}$ has its quotient-tower completion unit. Let $q_{A,HM}$ be precisely the one-letter comparison of [lem-sf-cbc-compact-support-composition-limit]: the diagram-site counit-tensor projection map for proper direct image, or the completed-open comparison defined by reduction of the completion unit.

Use the canonical derived scalar-restriction identifications $U_TA\cong\widetilde A U_V$, and $\rho_M:U_V\mathcal R_VM\cong\mathcal R_V^{\mathcal T}H_VM$, induced by the single strict quotient diagram and tensor reassociation. Write $\sigma_{A,M}:H_TA_{\rm int}M\xrightarrow{\sim}A_cH_VM$ for the identification by the canonical proper direct-image scalar comparison, respectively the completed-open identification fixed by the completion unit. Then the two maps from $U_T\mathcal R_T(A_{\rm int}M)$ to $\widetilde A\mathcal R_V^{\mathcal T}(H_VM)$ are equal:
$$ (\widetilde A\rho_M)\circ(U_TA\cong\widetilde A U_V)\circ U_T(r_{A,M})
 =q_{A,H_VM}\circ\mathcal R_T^{\mathcal T}(\sigma_{A,M})\circ\rho_{A_{\rm int}M}.$$
The scalar-restriction operation comparisons intertwine the units and counits of the proper inverse-image/direct-image and open-extension/restriction adjunctions, with inverse image the exact termwise inverse image on the ordinary derived system categories of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. The identifications and the displayed equality are natural in the derived strict-tower category, including the quotient transitions. No compactification-composition comparison is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0E48, remark-compatible-with-diagram, for compatibility of the counit-tensor projection map with change of ringed topoi. The strict varying-coefficient/constant-tower generator identification below is an additional agent-formulated obligation, not a verbatim assertion of the tag. The completion-unit normalization is the one in blueprint fix-lem-exchanges.proof.md Step 5 and lem-sf-cbc-compact-support-composition-limit.

proof.text: Work throughout with ordinary derived categories of strict systems. On the small diagram site of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], put $\mathcal A_T(n,W)=(A_n)_T(W)$ and $\mathcal B_T=\Delta\underline R_T$. Covers have fixed $n$, so a module over $\mathcal A_T$ is precisely a strict semilinear system: its integer-direction restrictions are the specified semilinear transitions. This identifies abelian categories exactly, hence their complex categories and localizations at quasi-isomorphisms. The identity-topos ringed map $v_T$ given by $\mathcal B_T\to\mathcal A_T$ has $E_T=-\otimes^L_{\mathcal B_T}\mathcal A_T\dashv U_T$, with exact restriction $U_T$ and the representative unit/counit of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. For $f:V\to T$, termwise $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ follows by transposing the transition equations; the module adjunction is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Since $f^{-1}(A_n)_T=(A_n)_V$ and $f^{-1}\underline R_T=\underline R_V$, these are ringed maps $f_a,f_b$ with exact pullbacks $F_a,F_b$ and $v_Tf_a=f_bv_V$. The ordinary unbounded derived adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] gives $F_a\dashv G_a=Rf_{a*}$ and $F_b\dashv G_b=Rf_{b*}$. By the current ordinary statement of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], $S_f$ is exactly this total right derived termwise direct image. These adjunctions are formed on all systems; the normalized objects are only the specified inputs.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition); ordinary ringed sequence-topos construction, as in lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to the two factorizations of the common ringed morphism $v_Tf_a=f_bv_V$. Since $Rv_{T*}=U_T$ and $Rv_{V*}=U_V$ are exact restriction, it gives a canonical isomorphism
$$d:U_TG_a\xrightarrow{\sim}G_bU_V.$$
This proves the required proper system operation comparison without asserting that restriction along $R\to A_n$ preserves K-injectives. Use [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] to normalize the corresponding pullback isomorphism
$$c:F_aE_T\xrightarrow{\sim}E_VF_b.$$
Its two composite adjunctions are identified by $c,d$, including their units and counits. These theorems apply on the small diagram sites just constructed and to unbounded complexes and nonflat structural ring maps. In particular $d$ is an actual derived strict-tower comparison, not a collection of evaluated arrows.

source.place: Tags 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), and 0FPI (lemma-adjoints-push-pull-compatibility); use the adjunction-normalized comparisons of the cited node

proof.text:
Identify the geometric inverse-image comparison $a:F_bU_T\xrightarrow{\sim}U_VF_a$ with the mate of $c^{-1}$ across $E_V\dashv U_V$ and $E_T\dashv U_T$. If $z_T:E_TU_T\to1$ is the scalar counit, this mate is the scalar adjunct of
$$E_VF_bU_TX\xrightarrow{c^{-1}}F_aE_TU_TX\xrightarrow{F_a z_{T,X}}F_aX.$$
To compute it, take a flat-term K-flat $\mathcal B_T$-resolution $Q\to U_TX$. By [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], the scalar counit is represented by $\mathcal A_T\otimes Q\to X$, $b\otimes q\mapsto bq$. The composite above is $b\otimes f^{-1}q\mapsto b f^{-1}q$; its scalar adjunct is the exact inverse image of $Q\to U_TX$. Because $F_b$ is exact, its localization is precisely the tautological isomorphism $a$. The representative and composition conventions are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], and the mate is the explicit Hom-bijection formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Thus this computes the comparison with its derived normalization; it does not apply scalar restriction to a chosen injective resolution. The resulting map is also the scalar-unit comparison $\tau$ specified in [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-restriction-counit], since the structural ring map is an isomorphism.

Apply [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-restriction-counit] to the diagram topoi of Step 1, with its constant ring $A=R$ and algebra sheaves $R_W=\mathcal A_W$. Its comparison $\kappa$ is exactly $d$: both are normalized by the two factorizations through the constant coefficient ring. Its scalar-unit comparison $\tau$ is exactly $a$: $f^{-1}\mathcal A_T=\mathcal A_V$, so its representative $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ is the inverse-image identity under the tensor unit isomorphism (also computed in Step 3). Its statement therefore gives
$$\epsilon^b_{U_VY}F_b(d_Y)=U_V(\epsilon^a_Y)a_{G_aY}.$$
By the transpose formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], this says that $d$ is the mate of $a$. The inverse mate word applied at $X$ gives
$$a_X=\epsilon^b_{U_VF_aX}F_b(d_{F_aX})F_bU_T(\eta^a_X).$$
Transpose this equation under $F_b\dashv G_b$ and use its triangle identity to obtain
$$d_{F_aX}U_T\eta^a_X=G_b(a_X)\eta^b_{U_TX}.$$
These are precisely the proper system counit and unit equations. The generic counit node allows arbitrary small ringed topoi, unbounded complexes, nonflat constant-to-algebra maps and nonconstant algebra sheaves, so it applies to the single varying-coefficient diagram ring; no etale or bounded-below specialization is being substituted.

Record the strict scalar reduction identification. Let $\Delta$ denote the constant tower and put $T_T=E_T\Delta$. The flatness and quotient assertions of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] give an isomorphism
$$k_X:\mathcal R_TX\xrightarrow{\sim}T_TH_TX$$
in the semilinear derived category, whose scalar restriction is $\rho_X$. Indeed take a flat-term K-flat completed-ring representative $Q$. Its restriction is K-flat over $\underline R_T$: for an acyclic $D$, $D\otimes_RQ=(D\otimes_R\widehat R_T)\otimes_{\widehat R_T}Q$ is acyclic by flatness of $\widehat R_T$ and K-flatness of $Q$. The terms are flat over $R$ by the same two exact tensor functors. The constant-diagram pullback sends this flat-term K-flat representative to $\Delta Q$, again flat-term K-flat by the same ringed-pullback theorem. Both reductions are therefore the single strict complex $(Q/t^nQ)_n$, as $\widehat R_T/t^n=(A_n)_T=\underline R_T/t^n$. The identifications send a class of $q$ to itself and commute with all quotient maps before localization. This is the ordinary derived reduction representative of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]; derived tensor and pullback are computed on these representatives by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. This gives $k$, including its naturality, rather than a lift of unrelated finite-level isomorphisms. The coefficient theorems apply with $A=R,I=(t)$: [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] makes $R$ a PID, hence Noetherian because every ideal is generated by one element. The quotients are finite by [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], so $R/(t)$ is additive torsion; $0\to R\xrightarrow{t^n}R\to A_n\to0$ is a finite-free resolution, since $R$ is a domain and $t\ne0$, so each quotient is perfect.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product) and 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); flatness and quotient properties are the additional complete-coefficient assertion cited

proof.text:
Check the constant-tower counit normalization needed below. Let $\chi_P:\Delta Rp_*P\xrightarrow{\sim}G_b\Delta P$ be [lem-sf-cbc-constant-tower-direct-image-normalization]. For $I=\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{op}$, there is exactly one arrow $n\to1$. Thus the formula for the evaluation right adjoint in [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] gives $e_{1*}=\Delta$, right adjoint to exact evaluation. It sends a K-injective complex $J$ to a K-injective tower by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. Choose a K-injective representative $J$ of $P$. The two sides of $\chi_P$ are then represented by the same tower $\Delta p_*J=p_*^{\mathcal T}\Delta J$, exactly as in clause (1) of the normalization node. Since inverse images here are exact, the corresponding derived counits are the underived counits on $J$ and $\Delta J$ by [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], with $s=t=f=1$ in its representative characterization of the counit at a K-injective target. Therefore
$$\epsilon^b_{\Delta P}F_b(\chi_P)=\Delta(\epsilon_P)$$
under $F_b\Delta\cong\Delta p^{-1}$, as an identity of chain maps of towers on these representatives. This proves the needed counit equation, rather than inferring it from the evaluated identity of $\chi$.

source.place: Tag 0FPI (lemma-adjoints-push-pull-compatibility); use the K-injective representative of the constant tower, with Tag 08BJ (derived-lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives)

proof.text:
For the proper case put $P=H_VM$ and $D=Rp_*P$. On diagram categories let $\chi:\Delta D\xrightarrow{\sim}G_b\Delta P$ be the constant-tower comparison of [lem-sf-cbc-constant-tower-direct-image-normalization]. Define a semilinear map
$$b:T_TD\longrightarrow G_aT_VP$$
as the $F_a\dashv G_a$ transpose of
$$F_aE_T\Delta D\xrightarrow{c}E_VF_b\Delta D\cong E_V\Delta p^{-1}D\xrightarrow{E_V\Delta\epsilon_P}E_V\Delta P.$$
The comparison involving $\Delta$ is the exact termwise inverse-image identity; Step 6 proves its counit compatibility with $\chi$. Thus all factors are actual diagram morphisms. After $d$, the scalar restriction of $b$ is exactly the diagram projection map $h_P:\mathcal R_T^{\mathcal T}D\to G_b\mathcal R_V^{\mathcal T}P$. In fact its $F_b$-transpose, using Step 4, is
$$U_V\epsilon^a\,a\,F_b(U_Tb)=U_V(\epsilon^a F_ab)\,a=U_V(E_V\Delta\epsilon_P)\,U_V(c)\,a.$$
The last composite, on a flat tensor model, sends $q\otimes\bar r$ to $\epsilon_P(q)\otimes\bar r$. This is precisely counit tensor identity after the pullback/tensor comparison, the defining transpose of $h_P$ in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Injectivity of the $F_b$-adjunction bijection proves $d\,U_Tb=h_P$. No invertibility of a projection map was used in this computation.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), and 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map); scalar-restriction equality is the displayed transpose computation, not Tag 0E48

proof.text:
Write $C_Z=\mathcal L_Z^{\mathcal T}\mathcal R_Z^{\mathcal T}$ and let $\eta_Z:1\to C_Z$ be the specified completion unit. Put
$$a_P:Rp_*C_VP\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_T^{\mathcal T}G_b\mathcal R_V^{\mathcal T}P.$$
This is the common-composite direct-image comparison of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. The normalizations in [lem-sf-cbc-constant-tower-direct-image-normalization] imply the equality
$$\mathcal L_T^{\mathcal T}(h_P)\eta_D=a_P\,Rp_*(\eta_P).\tag{*}$$
To see the whole-map equality, let $i_Z:\Delta Z\to\mathcal R^{\mathcal T}Z$ be the strict quotient map, and $\delta_Z:Z\to R\lim\Delta Z$ the constant-tower unit. Then $\eta_Z=R\lim(i_Z)\delta_Z$. Clause (4) gives $h_Pi_D=G_b(i_P)\chi_P$. Taking $R\lim$, using naturality of $a$ at $i_P$ and clause (3), $R\lim(\chi_P)\delta_D=a_{\Delta P}Rp_*(\delta_P)$, gives $(*)$ by substitution. This uses identities of derived tower maps, rather than uniqueness from their projections. The units here are the quotient-tower units of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence].

source.place: Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), with the strict-tower normalization clauses of the cited nodes

proof.text:
Let $X=A_{\rm int}M$, $N=S_p\mathcal R_VM$, and $P=H_VM$. The tower-definition identification is $d_A:\mathcal L_TN\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence]. Restrict the completed-ring limit, then use $d$ and $k_M$, to get
$$\lambda:H_T\mathcal L_TN\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_T^{\mathcal T}G_b\mathcal R_V^{\mathcal T}P.$$
For this restriction/limit comparison apply [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] to the identity-topos coefficient map; it applies to arbitrary underlying completed-ring towers. The proper scalar identification has the formula
$$\sigma_X=(a_P\,Rp_*\eta_P)^{-1}\lambda H_T(d_A^{-1}):H_TX\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*P.$$
Here $P$ is complete by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], so $\eta_P$ is invertible; $Rp_*$ preserves completeness by [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]. To identify this formula with the stipulated canonical proper direct-image scalar comparison, use [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] with $f=p$, coefficient ring $R$, and input $M$. Its strict reduction-tower comparison identifies the completed-ring K-injective direct image with the tower-defined $X$, and its final clause identifies scalar restriction of that direct image with $Rp_*H_VM$. These comparisons use the same derived-composition normalization and quotient unit as $\lambda$ and $a_P Rp_*\eta_P$. Reading its strict-tower comparison through $d_A$ therefore gives exactly the displayed formula. Thus $\sigma_X$ is the specified scalar comparison, rather than a newly chosen isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition); completion-reflector adjunction and actual integral reduction-tower normalization as in the cited statements

proof.text:
Using the semilinear lift of Step 7, form
$$b'_M=G_a(k_M^{-1})\,b\,T_T(\sigma_X)\,k_X:\mathcal R_TX\to N.$$
Its restricted map, after $d$ and $\rho_M$, is $h_P\mathcal R_T^{\mathcal T}(\sigma_X)\rho_X$. The $\mathcal R_T\dashv\mathcal L_T$ adjunct of $b'_M$ is $\mathcal L_T(b'_M)u_X$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Apply $H_T$ and $\lambda$ to this adjunct. Step 5 and the unit-preserving limit comparison identify the result with
$$\mathcal L_T^{\mathcal T}(h_P)\mathcal L_T^{\mathcal T}\mathcal R_T^{\mathcal T}(\sigma_X)\eta_{H_TX}
=\mathcal L_T^{\mathcal T}(h_P)\eta_D\sigma_X
=a_P Rp_*(\eta_P)\sigma_X
=\lambda H_T(d_A^{-1}),$$
using naturality of the completion unit, $(*)$, and the definition of $\sigma_X$. Both $X$ and $\mathcal L_TN$ are complete: $N$ is normalized by the item hypotheses, so [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] makes $\mathcal L_TN$ complete; use the isomorphism $d_A$ for $X$. The complete-coefficient equivalence is therefore faithful on these two objects. Cancel $\lambda$ and $H_T$ to see that the adjunct is $d_A^{-1}$. By the actual adjunction bijection, $b'_M=e_N\mathcal R_T(d_A^{-1})=r_{A,M}$ [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence]. Finally [lem-sf-cbc-compact-support-composition-limit] identifies $h_P$ with the prescribed proper $q_{A,P}$. This proves the full proper equality, including the constant-coordinate factor.

source.place: coefficient comparisons of the prescribed maps before taking adjunction mates

proof.text: For an open $j$, use the ordinary exact localized-site adjunction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Restriction of a module action leaves its extension-by-zero generators unchanged, so $U_TJ_j=J_jU_V$ and $H_Tj_!=j_!H_V$ on the underlying complexes; restriction to the open is the same equality. The open unit takes an open section to that same section, and the counit takes an extension generator over the open to its section on the ambient object. Forgetting the action leaves each of these maps unchanged. Thus these are equalities of the two exact adjunctions on complexes, hence on their derived localizations, including the strict integer transitions. This proves the open scalar unit/counit clause directly. It uses no infinite-limit claim about ordinary extension by zero. Put $Q=j_!P$ and $X=j_!M$. By [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison], $X$ is complete; restriction through the complete-coefficient equivalence makes $Q=H_TX$ complete. The canonical constant-coordinate identification is therefore $\sigma_X:H_TX=Q\xrightarrow{\eta_Q}C_TQ=J_j^cP$, with the actual completion unit.

source.place: open adjunction and completion-unit-normalized coefficient comparison

proof.text:
On the common flat-term completed-ring representative in Step 5, $r_j$ is the open tensor map of [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. Its scalar restriction, after $\rho$, is the strict constant-coordinate tensor comparison $q^{\rm tens}_{j,P}$. This is a whole-tower calculation: both adjuncts under the open extension/restriction adjunction send the extension generator $x\otimes\bar r$ to $x\otimes\bar r$ on the open. Replacing $\bar r$ by its image in $A_n$ gives the identical formula for every transition $A_m\to A_n$. Thus the chain maps of strict quotient systems agree before localization. The open-completion theorem [lem-sf-cbc-extension-zero-completion] states
$$q_{j,P}\mathcal R_T^{\mathcal T}(\eta_Q)=q^{\rm tens}_{j,P}.$$
Substitute $\sigma_X=\eta_Q$ from Step 11 and the reduction identification $\rho_X$; this gives exactly
$$J_j(\rho_M)(U_TJ_j\cong J_jU_V)U_Tr_j
=q_{j,P}\mathcal R_T^{\mathcal T}(\sigma_X)\rho_X.$$
The one-letter $q$ in [lem-sf-cbc-compact-support-composition-limit] is this same $q_j$. Its finite-level formula, used here with its strict transition normalization, is explicitly supplied by the extension-zero-completion statement.

source.place: canonical open tensor comparison and its completion-unit normalization

proof.text: All transformations used above are natural on the ordinary derived categories of the ringed sequence topoi. The proper comparison is formed from the derived composition comparisons on diagram ringed topoi, so its naturality is that of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]; $k$ and the completion units are natural strict quotient constructions of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]; and $q$ has the strict-tower naturality of [lem-sf-cbc-compact-support-composition-limit]. The proper unit and counit equalities were proved by the two adjunction Hom bijections in Step 4, and the open ones by the exact open adjunction in Step 11. Consequently their mates agree as well by substituting these equalities in the unit/comparison/counit formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. The finite cohomological/Tor intervals and compatible etale-origin witnesses are used only to remain in the domain of $d_A,r_A$ in [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence]; no stronger bounds or flatness of a finite quotient are assumed. Steps 1–4 construct the ordinary derived functors and their scalar-restriction mates; Steps 5–12 compute the specified quotient maps and actual adjunction transposes in those categories. Thus the ordinary derived route proves the assertion without an additional localization or section-realization interface. No assertion that evaluations detect equality of arbitrary derived arrows or any compactification-composition comparison occurs.
